request.spec: Return 'initials' as the upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot, e.g. 'J.S.'.
request.prompt:
Implement the following change to the application so that it fully satisfies
the specification and all existing and new tests pass. Run the test suite and
make it green before finishing.

Return 'initials' as the upper-cased first letters of firstName and lastName, dot-separated with a trailing dot, e.g. 'J.S.'.

agent.result_text:
`AcceptanceTest` is the only test class, and the full suite passes with `BUILD SUCCESS`.

## Summary

I implemented the `initials` derived field on the owner, following the existing `displayName` pattern:

1. **`src/main/resources/openapi.yml`** — added a read-only `initials` string property to the `Owner` schema, so the OpenAPI-generated `OwnerDto` includes the field (serialized into the GET response).

2. **`src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`** — added a `@Transient getInitials()` method returning the upper-cased first letters of `firstName` and `lastName`, dot-separated with a trailing dot (e.g. `"J.S."`). MapStruct auto-maps this getter onto the DTO just as it does `getDisplayName()`.

The acceptance test (`coreComputesInitials`, asserting `$.initials` == `"J.S."` for `john smith`) and the full suite pass: `Tests run: 1, Failures: 0, Errors: 0` — **BUILD SUCCESS**.

code_review.final_verdict:
VERDICT: LGTM

The `getInitials()` method sits right next to the existing derived display method on `Owner` (the one returning `lastName + ", " + firstName`), so it follows an established pattern in this exact class: a `@Transient`, computed, read-only accessor over the inherited name fields. That's the natural home a maintainer would expect, and it reuses the same `getFirstName()`/`getLastName()` accessors the sibling method uses rather than reaching into fields directly.

The OpenAPI addition mirrors the adjacent computed `readOnly` properties (same `title`/`description`/`type`/`example`/`readOnly` shape, placed among the other derived fields), so the schema change is consistent and additive too. No duplication, no catch-all growth — logic is in the right unit.
